To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

computerized measures of reaction time and conventional tests of memory and motor performance can detect cognitive changes in HIV-1-infested homosexual men, but that asymptomatic HIV- 1 seropositivity is not associated with cognitive abnormalities.

asymptomatic HIV‐1‐seropositive homosexual men do not show significant differences in neuropsychological test performance from seronegatives, but do show significant differences in test performance from symptomatic HIV‐1 seroposites.

(1) computerized neuropsychological assessment can be used as an effective and efficient tool for identifying cognitive changes in HIV-1 infection; (2) asymptomatic HIV- 1 seropositivity is not associated with a high rate of neuropsychological impairment; and (3) the frequency of neuropsycho logical impairment is significantly increased in symptomatic HIV‐1‐ seropositive individuals.

the identification of cognitive changes associated with HIV-1 infection and their relationship to the progression of the disease.
the use of computerized neuropsychological assessment in the evaluation of cognitive functioning in HIV-1-infested homosexual men.

the development of an objective, quantitative measure of cognitive functioning that is sensitive to the early effects of HIV-1 infection and that may be used as a screening instrument in clinical trials of new therapies for the treatment of HIV-1 disease.
